## Natural history notes

A large conehead katydid characterized by its long slender green to brown body, very long antennae, pointed cone-shaped head, and broad-tipped fastigium at the front of the head. In Florida, it is found in grassy wetlands, marsh edges, wet prairies, fields, roadsides, pine flatwoods, and other open habitats with tall grasses or sedges. It feeds mainly on grasses and other plant material, sometimes also taking small insects, and is most active at night when males call from vegetation while remaining well camouflaged among stems and blades.
